title: AI-Assisted Development: From Idea to Pull Request
location: 37 Normanby Road, Mount Eden, Auckland 1024, Auckland
description:
**AI-assisted development has moved far beyond autocomplete.**
Coding agents can now understand requirements, explore a codebase, work with development and design tools, build and test an app, fix failures, generate a pull request, and participate in code review.
At this meetup, we’ll explore practical end-to-end AI-assisted development workflows—from the initial idea and requirements to a tested, reviewable pull request.
**What we’ll explore**

* **Coding agents:** Codex, Claude, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and agentic capabilities in Xcode and other development environments
* **Project context:** Connecting agents to Jira, Linear, Confluence, documentation, and requirements
* **Design integration:** Working with Figma, Sketch, Zeplin, Penpot, Rive, design systems, components, and assets
* **Implementation:** Translating requirements and designs into production-ready code
* **Code review:** AI-assisted reviews, suggested changes, and automated fixes
* **Quality guardrails:** Unit tests, UI tests, snapshot tests, accessibility checks, and CI
* **Measuring results:** Code quality, rework, defects, build success, cost, and time to pull request
* **Responsible use:** Security, privacy, permissions, human oversight, and the limitations of coding agents

We’ll also discuss how developers, designers, QA, business analysts, and product teams can collaborate when AI agents become part of the development workflow.
**Interested in presenting?**
If you would like to present one of these topics—or another topic related to AI-assisted development—please contact me.
Short presentations, practical demonstrations, case studies, lessons learned, and honest accounts of unsuccessful experiments are all welcome.

We are currently exploring suitable venues and already have a couple of possible options.

title: Deep Dive into Jev & System One Models
description:
Looking for a chill but productive space to code, learn, and connect with other developers? Whether you’re just starting out or deep into a side project, you’re welcome here.

🔥 **This Fortnight's Spotlight: Jev & System One Models** Tired of wrestling with LLMs that hallucinate, break your JSON, and take 10 seconds to respond? This week, we're doing a quick 10-minute demo on **Jev** by TypeSafe AI—a brand new "System One" AI model.
Instead of acting like a chatbot that generates strings word-by-word, Jev acts like a lightning-fast function call. You give it unstructured data, and it outputs perfectly typed, probabilistic decisions in under 500 milliseconds. We'll look at why this parallel architecture is a game-changer for AI automation in your apps, and run a live demo of it in action.

🌟 **The Vibe & Details:** Alongside the demo, this remains a casual, community-driven space where you can:

• 💻 Work on your own coding projects
• 🎯 Share goals or progress (totally optional!)
• 🎙️ Talk tech, app development, and AI integration • ☕ Meet like-minded people over coffee

Come with your laptop, your curiosity, or just a love for tech. Stay for the connections and good vibes. No pressure, no strict schedule—just code, coffee, and vibes.

☕ *Note: This event is hosted at a local café, so we kindly ask that you support the venue by purchasing a drink or snack if you can.*

📅 We usually hold meetups every fortnight (bi-weekly)—use them to connect, share, and learn from others.

title: Footnote (Israel, 2012, 1 hr 47 mins)
description:
One of the absurdities of the crazy war in the Middle East is that Israel, Iran and Palestine all produce well made films that depict beautifully the human condition with all our complexities. loves and frailties and or common humanity. In our film club we have seen these films. How can humans possibly fight each other? Why?

In this tragi-comic film, a father and son are both professors at the same university in Jerusalem. They have a classic love/hate relationship. We don't necessarily end up siding with either of them, as neither really gain our full sympathy. But we "get" them and that is the genius of the film.

Some reviews:
“Footnote requires little knowledge of Judaism and its texts. Rather, it's about the complications of love, guilt, and rage.” The New Yorker
It's not easy to make Eliezer a sympathetic character, yet Bar-Aba's demonstration of fleeting vulnerability awakens inevitable, if equally brief, compassion.” Washington Post
“This is brainy, bravura filmmaking of the highest level, a motion picture that is as difficult to pigeonhole as it is a pleasure to enjoy.” Los Angeles Times
“Shows just what you can do with a carefully constructed plot and lovingly drawn characters - even if, in the end, neither of them is particularly lovable.” London Evening Standard

Nominated for an Oscar as Best Foreign Language Film and won the prize for screenplay at Cannes
